body:
Applicable host-contract version: generation 1 (HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION = 1), asserted via assertHostContract(1).

Evidence and reasoning:
1. Exact pinned artifact governs. package.json and pnpm-workspace.yaml pin @ordarium/core and @ordarium/host-kit to the ordarium-v1.3.1 release tarballs. The installed @ordarium/core 1.3.1 ships dist/src/host.d.ts with `export declare const HOST_CONTRACT_VERSION = 1` and dist/src/host.js implementing `assertHostContract(v)` as exact-match, fail-closed (throws HostContractMismatchError on any other value). @ordarium/host-kit 1.3.1 is only a curated re-export of that handshake from core. Per docs/engineering/08-source-precedence-policy.md rule 1, the published contract of the exact pinned version governs the interface.
2. Workspace integration matches. src/effects/runtime.ts:128 calls `assertHostContract(1)` at assembly and exposes the pass-through `hostPort`; test/host_conformance.test.ts (CONF-A01) asserts assertHostContract(1) passes and assertHostContract(2) throws. docs/engineering/13-host-adapter-conformance-spec.md freezes the same "contract generation 1".
3. The only dissenting source is docs/engineering/notes/host-contract-note.md, which records "2" but explicitly marks itself "informational, not normative". Under docs/08 rules 3, informational records are explanatory only and never override the pinned published contract (or the project's normative spec). There is no source anywhere in the workspace (docs, lock/pins, or installed artifacts) indicating a generation-2 bump.

Conclusion: the conflict is apparent, not genuine — provenance/scope (non-normative note vs. shipped pinned contract) plus the local source-precedence rule resolve it locally, so no peer contact was required. The host contract generation applying to this integration is 1. Note that the pins were advanced to ordarium-v1.3.1 (later than the 1.2.0 recorded in docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md), but the contract generation at that pin is still 1, so the answer is unchanged.
